extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors and referees submitting to The American Mathematical Monthly (MAA)
extracted.subtask_description: Author and referee guidance for preparing and submitting manuscripts, problems, and book reviews to The American Mathematical Monthly, including scope, required templates, submission types, and review policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priorities for articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Mathematical Monthly prioritizes articles that are clear, informative, engaging, and accessible to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Monthly is an international, peer-reviewed journal publishing high-quality, original expository research read by PhD students, faculty, and math enthusiasts. Articles cover a wide range of mathematical topics including expositions of old or new results, historical or biographical essays, speculations, definitive treatments, broad developments, or explorations of single applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Mathematical Monthly only publishes manuscripts in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Mathematical Monthly has a double-anonymous review policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare submissions consistent with double-anonymous review (i.e., remove identifying information when appropriate); referees should follow the journal's refereeing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission types
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Mathematical Monthly accepts the following types of articles: Articles, Notes, Problems and Solutions, Book Reviews, Mathbits, Letters to the Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose the appropriate category when preparing submissions and consult templates/style files relevant to the category (article, note, filler, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX style file and template requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please download and use the LaTeX Style File with the article, note, and filler templates before submitting it to The American Mathematical Monthly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New submissions must include a title page and cover letter. There are updates to the instructions and the article/note template; more information is available in the README Author Instructions downloadable with the templates and styleguide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page and cover letter required for new submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: New submissions must include a title page and cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See README Author Instructions included with the templates for details about what to include in the title page and cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems and Solutions submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem proposals must be accompanied by solutions. Submitted problems should not be under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems and Solutions is consistently the most downloaded section of the Monthly; submit original problems that will appeal to the readers of the Monthly and include full solutions with the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow the journal's 'Instructions for Figures' when preparing illustrations for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific figure formatting and submission requirements are provided in the linked 'Instructions for Figures' document (authors should consult that document for technical details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereeing for the American Mathematical Monthly is governed by a 'Guide for Referees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees and editors should consult the Guide for Referees for standards and expectations when evaluating submissions; authors may infer evaluation criteria from that guide and from the journal's stated priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book review handling and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Monthly accepts Book Reviews; Darren Glass is the Book Review Editor (contact: glassd@dickinson.edu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors or reviewers interested in contributing a book review should contact the Book Review Editor for instructions and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint permission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: General permission is granted to institutional members of the MAA for noncommercial reproduction in limited quantities of individual articles (in whole or in part) provided a complete reference is made to the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprint permission should be requested from Taylor and Francis; use the provided reprint request form and follow Taylor & Francis contact procedures for permissions.
